SIKAGROUT®-9130: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: SikaGrout®-9130, July 2025, Version 02.01 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/6/sikagrout-9130.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide SikaGrout®-9130 where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (July 2025, Version 02.01).
1.2 Product description. SikaGrout®-9130 is a shrinkage-compensated, cement-based grout for onshore wind turbine installations that, when mixed with water, forms a flowable, cohesive, and impermeable grout with rapid high compressive strength. Featuring advanced nano-engineered binder technology, this grout blends Portland and special cements to deliver exceptional structural performance. Offering excellent flowability, SikaGrout®-9130 is suitable for narrow constrictions such as grout trenches for onshore wind turbines.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. SikaGrout®-9130 has been especially formulated for:
    - Grouting of wind turbine installations, that are installed using pre-stressing techniques e.g. base plate grouting of onshore wind turbines
    - Installations where excellent fatigue resistance is required
    - Onshore turbines where ultra-high final strengths are required
    - Grouting in a wide temperature range
    - Anchoring anchor bolts of wind turbine towers
    - All void filling from 25mm to 600mm (under tower flange) where high strength, high modulus, high ductility is important
    Contact the Technical Department of your local Sika office regarding any application or dimensions required not mentioned here.
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.10.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. SikaGrout®-9130
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: One component, ultra-high early and final strength, shrinkage compensated, cementitious grout for onshore wind turbine installations
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Certificates and test reports.
    - Tests on fresh and hardened grouting mortar - verification by MPA Hannover
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).

    - EN 206: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Compressive strength (p.2).
    - EN 12390-13: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Modulus of elasticity in compression (p.2).
    - ASTM C469: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Modulus of elasticity in compression (p.2).
    - EN 1015-11: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Flexural-strength (p.2).
    - ASTM C882: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Shear adhesion strength (p.2).
    - EN 12390-6: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Splitting tensile strength (p.2).
    - ASTM C1437: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Application Information > Flowability (p.3).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Ultra-high compressive strength: above highest class of EN206, i.e. > C100/115
    - Ultra-high modulus for exceptional stiffening properties
    - Excellent fatigue resistance
    - Quick return to service and removal of temporary supports due to high early strength build-up ≥ 70 MPa @ 24hrs at 20°
    - No segregation or bleeding to ensure consistent final physical performance and to prevent pump blockages.
    - Extended pot life of ≈ 3 hours
    - Can be pumped into complex areas or areas inac-cessible to conventional grouting methods.
    - Ultra-high Young’s modulus for exceptional stiffness
    - No segregation or bleeding
    - Shrinkage compensated
    - Good flowability
    Contact the Technical Department of your local Sika office regarding any application at temperatures 35 oC to 45 oC.
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Density: 2.39 - 2.45 ton/m³ (EN 12390-7)
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.

    - Flexural-strength: >18.0 N/mm² (EN 1015-11)
    - Splitting tensile strength: 7.5 N/mm² (EN 12390-6)

2.10 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: SikaGrout®-9130 is supplied in special 25 kg bags and 500, 1000, 1500 kg big bags
    - Shelf life: 12 months from date of production
2.11 Storage conditions. Product must be stored in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging in dry conditions away from direct sunlight and heat, not exceeding 40 oC. When stored under high temperature and high humidity conditions, the shelf life may be reduced.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (July 2025, Version 02.01) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality.
    - Concrete
    - The concrete must be structurally sound, thoroughly clean, free from oil, grease, dust, loose material, surface contamination and materials which will impair the grout flow or reduce adhesion strength. Laitance, delaminated, weak, damaged and deteriorated concrete and where necessary sound concrete must be removed by suitable mechanical preparation as directed by the engineer or supervising officer. Any pockets or holes for structural fixings must also be cleaned of all debris.
3.3 Substrate quality - Shutter Formwork. Where formwork is to be used, all formwork must be of adequate strength, treated with release agent and sealed to prevent leakage of pre-wetting water and grout. Ensure formwork includes outlets for removal of the pre-soaking water or use vacuum extraction equipment to remove water.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (July 2025, Version 02.01) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: 7.5 to 9.2 % water / powder ratio
    - Consumption: Approximately 450 liters per ton material
    - Layer thickness: 25 - 600 mm
    - Pot Life: 3 hours
4.3 Flowability.
    | Flow channel | > 610 mm |
    | Flow cone | > 285 mm |
    | Flow class | f1 |
    | Classification according to DAfStb Richtlinie |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: (ASTM C1437; EN
    Test method printed: 13395-2)
4.4 Notes on installation.
    - SikaGrout®-9130 has been especially formulated for use in specific applications. As such SikaGrout®-9130 should be installed by experienced fully trained contractors. Full application procedures are available on request.
    - Sands or other products that could affect the products properties must not be added.
    - SikaGrout®-9130 which will be exposed to strong drying conditions, e.g. mortar which is directly exposed to heavy wind and/or direct sunlight, should be protected using appropriate curing agents.
4.5 Equipment.
    | Mixer type | Paddle mixer |
    | Mixing time | Approximately 6 minutes |
    | Application method | One continuous pour |
4.6 Mixing.
    - Grout mixer
    - SikaGrout®-9130 must be mixed using suitable grout mixing equipment combined with agitator for continuous large volume mixing. Volume capacity of equipment must be applicable to the volume of material being mixed for a continuous operation. Equipment trials must be considered to ensure product can be mixed satisfactory before full project application. Put most of the water required in the mixer and add slowly the grout material. Mix until a homogeneous mortar (3 to 4 minutes), add the remaining water and continue mixing for at least another 2 minutes until the required fluid or flowable consistency is obtained. Mix with potable water only. Do not add more water than the maximum specified. Note: Do not use continuous mixing equipment.
4.7 Application.
    - Strictly follow installation procedures as defined in method statements, application manuals and working instructions which must always be adjusted to the actual site conditions. Pre-wetting
    - The prepared concrete substrate must be thoroughly saturated with clean water for a recommended 12 hours before application of the grout. The surface must not be allowed to dry within this time. Prior to application of the grout, all water must be removed from within formwork, cavities or pockets and the final surface must achieve a dark matt appearance (saturated surface dry) without glistening.
    - Placing: Grout pump application
    - For large volume placement, grout pumps are recommended. Equipment trials must be considered to ensure product can be pumped satisfactory.
    - Surface finishing
    - Finish exposed grout surfaces to the required surface texture as soon as the grout has started to stiffen. Do not add additional water on the surface. Do not over work surface as this may cause surface discoloration and cracking. After the grout has initially hardened, remove formwork and trim edges while concrete is ‘green’.
    - Cold weather working
    - Consider storing bags in a warm environment and using warm water to assist with achieving strength gain and maintaining physical properties.
    - Hot weather working
    - Consider storing bags in a cool environment and using cold water to assist with controlling the exothermic reaction to reduce cracking and maintaining physical properties.
4.8 Curing treatment. Protect exposed grout surfaces after finishing (immediately after levelling) from premature drying and cracking by curing under water for at least 72 hours. In cold weather apply insulated blankets to maintain a constant temperature to prevent surface damage from freezing and frost.
4.9 Cleaning of equipment. Tools and spillages can be cleaned with water while SikaGrout®-9130 is still uncured. Once hardened, the material can only be removed mechanically.
4.10 Limitations and important considerations.
    - To avoid cracking of exposed surfaces, protect from direct sun and, or strong wind.
    - Use only on clean, sound substrate.
    - The substrate must be free of ice.
    - Do not exceed water addition.
    - Protect freshly applied material immediately.
    - Keep exposed surfaces to a minimum. To avoid cracking in warm temperatures keep bags cool & use cold water for mixing.
    - Do not use vibrating pokers.
    - Do not use continuous mixing equipment.
    - Pour or pump from one side only. Avoid exposing surfaces during rainfall and prior to final set.
4.11 . (formerly NaX® Q130)
4.12 Further documentation. Sika Method Statement: SikaGrout®-9130

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Material temperature. 0 °C min. / +35 °C max.
5.3 Ambient air temperature. 0 °C min. / +35 °C max.
5.4 Substrate temperature. 0 °C min. / +35 °C max.
5.5 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.10):
    - To avoid cracking of exposed surfaces, protect from direct sun and, or strong wind.
    - Keep exposed surfaces to a minimum. To avoid cracking in warm temperatures keep bags cool & use cold water for mixing.
5.6 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Density: 2.39 - 2.45 ton/m³ (EN 12390-7)
    - Compressive strength: Age | N/mm²; 1 day | > 70; 3 days | > 95; 7 days | > 110; 28 days | > 130; 56 days | > 140; 50 mm & 75 mm cubes results at 20 oC; Age | N/mm²; 1 day | > 70; 3 days | > 80; 7 days | > 90; 28 days | > 110; 56 days | > 120; 150 x 300 mm cylinder results; Compressive strength class | > C100/115; Early strength classification | A; Exposure classes | XC4, XD3, XS3, XF3, XA2,; WF (ASTM C109/C109M; EN 12390-3) (EN 12390-3) (EN 206)
    - Modulus of elasticity in compression: 48.000 N/mm²; Poisson's ratio: 0.19 (EN 12390-13) (ASTM C469)
    - Flexural-strength: >18.0 N/mm² (EN 1015-11)
    - Shrinkage: 91 days | < ‰ 0.15 (ASTM C1090/C1090M)
    - Shear adhesion strength: 14 days | 40.0 N/mm2 (ASTM C882)
    - Splitting tensile strength: 7.5 N/mm² (EN 12390-6)
    - Flowability: Flow channel | > 610 mm; Flow cone | > 285 mm; Flow class | f1; Classification according to DAfStb Richtlinie (ASTM C1437; EN 13395-2)
5.7 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.8 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: SikaGrout®-9130, July 2025, Version 02.01, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/6/sikagrout-9130.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
